title: Fifty terminals benchmarked against the published latency budgets

cases.summary: IDEAL profile (16 PTYs, 8 writable control-event clients plus one non-reader, 16 requests in flight, 1 MiB/s aggregate output, 10000 measured samples after 1000 explicit warmup samples): every admission sample and every commit-to-written event sample, warmup included, is <= 100 ms, no event to a writable client is lost or unwritten, peak RSS <= 1 GiB and history disk <= 4 GiB. Capacity profile (50 PTYs, 400 output viewers): admission and event p99 <= 100 ms, reported separately and labelled capacity-release-target, never as the IDEAL assumption. Both report p50/p95/p99/max, counts, rejected work, CPU, RSS, disk, per-client and per-viewer lag, host and build facts and the binary hash; raw samples are kept beside the evidence. The verdict also fails when fewer terminals, viewers, writable clients or request lanes actually ran than the profile requests (requested and realized shapes are both reported), and a capacity run with any shape other than 50/8/16/1 MiB/s is refused as usage.

With every control-event writer delayed 150 ms the IDEAL run exits 1 with budget_exceeded: event_max_ms reports the slow samples (all >= 150 ms) against the unchanged 100 ms budget; no sample is filtered and the budget is not widened. The admission-side fixture {"fixture":"admission-delay","delay_ms":150} likewise exits 1 with admission_max_ms over the unchanged budget, every sample kept.

verified_in_crate: cargo run --locked --release --manifest-path bench/Cargo.toml --bin terminal50 -- (the commands above)
